title: Bubbles reintroduces Chuck at the Apollo youth fund show
summary: In 1960 at a charity youth fund night at the Apollo, John Bubbles tells the audience Chuck and Chuckles are back and Green dances Lady Be Good.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Let's move on a bit. When was the next time you did -- started dancing professionally as a tap dancer, and under what circumstances?
It was under this -- it was for the youth fund. At the Apollo Theater, at one 125 Street.

1960. I was being reintroduced by the father of rhythm, I call him the jeweler of the pages. John W. Bubbles. He's number one 'Sporting Life' for Porgy and Bess. And he sang, he told the ladies and gentlemen of the audience he said, that I was back. Chuck and Chuckles. You see, and he was -- he was involved in some kind of a tuition at the time, because these publishers of Amsterdam News and Jet Magazine, Johnson Publications, you see, Ebony, and I think they had another world going too, and in those days and 60 I think, so they had discontinued and backstage at the Apollo Theater, they was clamoring, everyone wanted to do their part,

you see? Oh, you had some of the best there is in the world, you see, and the show they only had -- they had a time limit, they was limited to about three hours, I think, something like that, till midnight. And, I -- well see he died, he was -- he was a favorite, John W. Bubbles. See. And he -- he sang 'Lady Be Good' and told the ladies and the gentlemen, he was going to sing 'Lady Be Good' and then that Chuck Green was coming out of Chuckie and Chuckles, and dance.

So, that's what happened, but in the -- during the -- the show, the performance, the youth fund show, it was a charity and he had to go down under the stage you see, to these publications, you know, they was -- take some photographs or some pictures, I say, do some footage. And, with these other businesses. And, in the meantime I'm trying to get off, trying to finish my dance, I was tap dancing, I call it lunches, you see, and of the melodies, of the titles, 'Lady Be Good,' so I would do a tap dance on lunches, you see and -- I came off the audience started applauding, right? And had SRO, and turnaway go -- crowds and I didn't see Mr. Bubbles.

So I said, number one in the world, where are you? You understand, and someone said he went down the stairs. The steps, you know. So I knew what they meant by he went down the steps. So I went -- they was in the band room, you see? So I went down there and there he was sure enough, he was -- he was doing another footage, you know, the photographer

was taking pictures of him in the -- and the VIP's, you see very important persons, you see? So I says, number one in the world, I mean, the audiences wants us, I said, we have to take a bow, we have to bow together. You see? So, think he -- said, I'm right with you. So we went up and we went out back into the lights. And took another bows, you see, and then we came off into other crossings and he went and continued his -- ah -- ah, you know, he was doing this footages.

You see? Now I think it was all for the better, everyone was satisfied, AGVA president was there, Mr. Joey Adams, you know. And I think he made excuses for Lou Buck, you see. Little Lou Buck, generally he had him on a tour with him once. Little Lou Buck, you know was a tap dancer.
